metadata.title: Regional cerebral palsy prevalence reference dataset
metadata.method: Static regional GeoJSON used for choropleth display. Values are representative published prevalence ranges, not patient-level surveillance data.
sources: CDC: Cerebral palsy affects about 1 in 345 children in the United States.
Cerebral Palsy Foundation: approximately 17 million people live with cerebral palsy worldwide.
Published population studies commonly report around 2-3.5 cerebral palsy cases per 1,000 live births, with regional variation.

properties.name: North America
properties.childrenEstimate: CDC reports about 1 in 345 U.S. children.
properties.note: Shown as a regional reference; surveillance systems differ by country.

properties.name: Latin America
properties.childrenEstimate: Estimated from published prevalence ranges by live births.
properties.note: Reliable country-level CP registries are limited across this region.

properties.name: Europe
properties.childrenEstimate: Estimated from CP registry prevalence ranges.
properties.note: Several European countries maintain mature CP surveillance registries.

properties.name: Africa
properties.childrenEstimate: Estimated from higher published prevalence ranges where neonatal risk and care access vary.
properties.note: Measured prevalence can be undercounted where surveillance is limited.

properties.name: Asia
properties.childrenEstimate: Estimated from published prevalence ranges by live births.
properties.note: Large regional differences are expected; this is a broad reference band.

properties.name: Oceania
properties.childrenEstimate: Estimated from Australian and regional prevalence reporting.
properties.note: Australia has relatively strong CP registry reporting compared with many regions.
properties.source: Australian CP Register and published studies
